# A Julia Figure

The cell below emits a PNG figure as a **file** (not an inline base64
data-URI). The key is *how the value is shown*, not where the bytes come from:

1. The cell returns a `PngFigure` wrapper that is showable **only** as
   `image/png` (it defines a single `Base.show(::MIME"image/png")` method and
   no `text/html` one). QuartoNotebookRunner therefore captures only the
   `image/png` MIME; q2's `displayDataMimeType` selects it (a value that is
   *also* `text/html`-showable would be emitted inline instead — see the 4CD
   MIME finding), and the jupyter `toMarkdown` image branch (`mdImageOutput`)
   writes the figure to `plot_files/figure-html/*.png`, referencing it via
   `<img src=...>`.
2. The PNG bytes are a small pre-rendered line chart, embedded as base64 and
   decoded with the `Base64` **stdlib**. Using a hardcoded image (rather than a
   `Plots.jl` `savefig`) keeps this fixture **dependency-free**: the notebook
   environment needs no external packages, so the page renders on a cold Julia
   depot (e.g. CI, which has no warm `~/.julia`) with no `Pkg.instantiate`.
   q2's figure-file handling is identical regardless of the byte source — this
   fixture exercises that path, not Plots.

```{julia}
using Base64

# A ~140x90 PNG line chart (axes + a blue sine polyline), base64-encoded.
const FIGURE_PNG_BASE64 = ""

struct PngFigure
    bytes::Vector{UInt8}
end
Base.show(io::IO, ::MIME"image/png", f::PngFigure) = write(io, f.bytes)

PngFigure(base64decode(FIGURE_PNG_BASE64))
```
